chunks: From him, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Should I marry off a young girl who is three years old, or should I marry off a boy who is three years old, and what is the minimum age at which they can be married?' He said: 'When the girl reaches maturity and does not consent to the marriage, what is her status?' He said: 'There is no harm in that, provided her father or her guardian consented.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a father marrying off his young daughter before she reaches maturity, and does she have the right to reject it later?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the validity of 'nikah al-sighr' (child marriage) contracted by the father or guardian before the girl reaches puberty. He confirms that the initial contract is binding and valid based on the guardian's consent, but grants the girl the right of 'khiyar al-bulugh' (option of maturity) to annul it if she chooses not to remain in the marriage upon reaching maturity. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that while the father holds the authority to contract the marriage, the girl's consent becomes a decisive factor for the marriage's continuity after she attains legal capacity.
